claim: E-PN6-nomad-per-node failed at splitter verification (haiku splitter rejected twice in a row, run halted) — pipeline terminated at $0.37 before any node was attempted. The LLM router startup decision MATCHED E029 exactly (designer+coder=sonnet, rest=haiku, splitter=haiku); the failure was that the haiku splitter's split proposals couldn't pass the verifier twice. E029 ran the SAME config and the haiku splitter passed. E-PN4-nomad-rerun also ran the same and passed. This is run-to-run variance in haiku splitter outputs — n=1 unlucky failure, not a routing-logic defect. INCONCLUSIVE on the per_node_routing=true question for nomad2018.

support.llm_router_startup_decision: Same as E029: designer+coder=sonnet, rest including splitter=haiku

failure.cause: RuntimeError: splitter agent failed verification twice; halting run.
failure.interpretation: Haiku splitter produced bad splits two attempts in a row; engine halted the run to protect downstream coders. E029 and E-PN4-nomad-rerun also used haiku splitter and PASSED — this is unlucky run-to-run variance for haiku-on-splitter, not a routing-logic issue.

scope: INCONCLUSIVE — pipeline aborted before any per-node decision could be made. Not a per-node routing test.

implications.design_finding: Haiku-splitter on nomad2018 has run-to-run failure rate. n=2 success / n=1 failure across E029, E-PN4-nomad-rerun, E-PN6 — non-trivial fail rate. Static rule candidate: bump splitter from haiku to sonnet on tabular-regression to stabilize.
implications.next_experiment: Pivot to a fresh design test: LLM router on detecting-insults. E020 showed detecting requires opus-everywhere ($342). Does the agent READ E020/E026 and pick opus-all (smart)? Or does it overlook the evidence and pick a cheaper config that will fail? This tests the agent's evidence-following ability on a task where the right answer is expensive.

next_actions: Launch E-PN7-detecting: router_strategy=llm + per_node_routing=false on detecting-insults. Tests agentic reasoning on a task where the right answer is opus-everywhere ($342).
